Subject: Overdue Library Book Notice

Dear Student,

We hope you're doing well. Our records show that you currently have an overdue book: "The Great Gatsby" by F. Scott Fitzgerald (call number PS3511.I9 G7). It was due on March 10. As of today, you've accrued a late fee of $2.50 ($0.50 per day). To avoid additional charges, please return the book by March 15. After that date, a $5.00 processing fee will be applied. If the book is not returned by March 20, it will be considered lost, and a $15.00 replacement fee will be charged.

You can return the book to the circulation desk at Anderson Library during regular hours (8:00 AM – 10:00 PM) or use the external book drop near the main entrance at any time. If you have any questions, please contact Library Circulation at libcirc@university.edu or call 555-0198.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Best regards,
Library Circulation Services

questions.explanation: The email primarily asks the student to return the overdue book and details the fees and deadlines, making option C the correct main purpose.

Subject: Shift Swap Request – Friday Library Desk

Hi Alex,

I'm writing to see if you'd be willing to swap shifts with me this week. I'm scheduled for Friday from 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM at the library front desk, but I have a study session for my biology exam. I see you're scheduled for Tuesday from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the same desk. Could you take my Friday shift? I can cover your Tuesday one. The pay rate is $12.50 per hour.

I've already checked with our supervisor, Ms. Parker, and she said a swap is okay as long as we both agree and submit the online form through the employee portal by Wednesday at 5:00 PM. Also, I can share my study notes for Dr. Chen's class if you'd like.

Let me know by tomorrow evening. Thanks!

Best,
Jamie

Notice: E-Waste Recycling Drive

The University Facilities Office, in collaboration with GreenTech Recycling, is pleased to announce our annual e-waste recycling drive. It will be held on Saturday, April 22, from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM in Parking Lot B behind Anderson Hall (enter via Maple Drive).

Accepted items include:
• Computers, laptops, and monitors (CRT monitors subject to a $5.00 fee)
• Printers, scanners, and keyboards
• Mice, cables, phones, and tablets
• Small appliances (e.g., toasters, fans)

Items not accepted: refrigerators, air conditioners, batteries, and hazardous materials.

Participants are requested to arrive with items already removed from their vehicles. Volunteers will be available to assist with unloading. Please note: The university cannot guarantee data destruction; it is the responsibility of the participant to erase all personal data prior to drop-off. E-waste from off-campus sources will not be accepted.

This event is free for all items except CRT monitors. For inquiries, contact the Office of Sustainability at sustainability@univ.edu or call 555-0223. Thank you for contributing to a greener campus.

questions.stem: According to the notice, what items are NOT accepted at the e-waste drive?
questions.explanation: The notice explicitly lists refrigerators and batteries as items not accepted.

options.A: pay a $5.00 fee for each item
options.D: erase all personal data from devices

questions.explanation: The notice states: 'it is the responsibility of the participant to erase all personal data prior to drop-off.'

options.A: to announce a fee increase for CRT monitors

options.C: to request volunteers for the recycling event
options.D: to explain data security policies for electronic devices

questions.explanation: The notice primarily provides details about the upcoming e-waste recycling drive, encouraging participation.

Subject: Volunteer for WUCR 88.5 FM – Spring Semester Openings

Dear Students,

Are you interested in radio broadcasting? WUCR 88.5 FM is now recruiting volunteers for the spring semester. We're looking for on-air hosts, news reporters, music directors, and production assistants. No previous experience is required—we'll train you. Benefits include practical broadcasting experience, a professional demo reel, and a $10 per hour stipend for on-air shifts.

Volunteers must commit at least 3 hours per week. Training sessions will be held the week of March 6. There will be an info session on Thursday, March 2, at 6:00 PM in the Student Union, Room 203. If you cannot attend, you can apply online at wucr.edu/volunteer by March 1. On-air hosts must complete a separate technical orientation.

For more information, contact Maria, recruitment coordinator, at maria@wucr.edu. We can't wait to hear your voice on the air!

Best wishes,
The WUCR Team
